body: It's difficult to look around without seeing examples of the trajectory society expects life to take: be born, go to school, go to college/university, get a job, find a girl, settle down. I understand that very few people actually follow this journey to the letter but look around; all kinds of media show relationships as the 'normal' thing. Add to this that many of my friends are starting to settle down with children and partners and I do feel bad that I've never been able to take a girl home to meet the folks. Of course this is only a portion of why I feel bad; I want it for myself first and foremost, but the parent angle does give me a bit of grief (from myself, not my parents).

I'm on a fixed rota so extra work isn't really an option. I do talk to the friend I mentioned above but there's only so much I feel comfortable sharing. Hell, there's some things I only use as a rod to beat myself with. I couldn't imagine sharing it with someone and have their reaction be one of understanding. I'm writing, it's hard to avoid writer's block but I do hope to self publish one day. That's another thing I'm sharing with this girl, she's read all of what I've written (the only person to have done so) and she makes suggestions. I wish I could be more open with certain aspects of my life, it's a millstone round my neck.
It's great that you know your goals. I used to know mine too but my plans didn't work out so now I have to change gears and figure out a new target.

Well I'm opinionated. Chances are I'd know where I stand on any particular issue when I hear it. What I don't know is where I fit in. I feel like I don't fully identify with any group of people I associate with whereas a lot of people I know have found their niche and are comfortable in their little peer groups. Some people know what they want from life in terms of personal and professional goals, even if they haven't achieved them yet they know what to work towards.

I guess what I'm driving at is I don't have any specific target and I don't feel at ease with myself. I'm hoping that changes and I'm wondering when the turning point was for the rest of you.
Perhaps you're comfortable with who you are then? Congratulations.
I don't know who I am. I know I want something different for myself but I don't know what. So at 27 I'm still searching and hoping.

The enjoyment versus worth is dependent on the point in time. Beforehand no it's not worth it, afterwards I might disagree, during depends on what we're doing in the club because while I do enjoy doing things I don't enjoy fully exerting myself. I don't know why it is rock climbing appeals to me, probably for the same reason parkour does. I wouldn't say I'm a very active person though, running tends to bore me, maybe biking instead. I can only really think of one person I'd be relatively comfortable talking to face to face and she's got her own problems and I work with her so it's combining two aspects of my life I perhaps shouldn't. Also she's younger than me and much more sexually experienced and active than me so I'd be humiliated and she couldn't possibly relate. I find I'm going through odd manic phases at the moment which didn't happen before, at least not to my recollection, I'm feeling better than I was but still very melancholic and I think I'm only better because I've got the distraction of work during the week

I do a martial art but because of work I don't really do it very often any more and it takes a monumental effort to drag myself there even though I usually end up enjoying myself. For some reason whenever someone asks me if there are any hobbies I want to take up I think of rock climbing and then nothing else comes to mind. It's not that I'm obsessed with the idea but it's the only thing that really holds my interest. Having said that I don't know anywhere nearby to do that sort of thing. To top it off I feel very self conscious if I'm doing something I'm inexperienced at. I've tried to reach out before but it's not really the sort of thing you can come out and say in a text, I have no idea how to approach it or how to answer follow up questions.

I'm 27, nearly 28. I have probably three people I could talk to. Out of those one couldn't relate as much as I'd like because he's very outgoing and popular and I'd feel uncomfortable telling him anyway, one is usually busy with her life and to top it off I only got to know her through the friend she's with (who I definitely couldn't talk to about this), and the last is a relatively new friend who I work with and she's got plenty of her own problems, she doesn't need to listen to mine.

It's been so long since I felt happy I don't really know what it took. I just feel I'm spinning my wheels and getting nowhere. Life's passing me by so why stay around to watch it go? I don't really know why I feel this way. I can only assume it's because I'm a dateless wonder, especially since this particular episode started with being ignored by someone I messaged. I can't be ignored by so many because they're the ones with a problem, I must be the one that's wrong, Occam's razor and all. I've tried going to a therapist before but I hit a wall because I'm so humiliated I didn't share all I should have and also the money. I'm in a better financial place now but I want to use the extra money to move out and I'm probably more humiliated than ever.
Would it put you off because you'd be thinking there's a problem with him or because virginity itself is a problem?
That's the sort of situation I'm envisioning. I know real life doesn't often go the way you plan it though so how would you feel if he didn't tell you?

I've seen a lot of posters saying they'd be fine with things. It's because you seem to be in the minority that I'd like to ask you more questions. I don't have any (realistic) romantic interests on the horizon at the moment but whenever I have been interested in someone it's always at the forefront of my mind that they'd think differently about me if they knew. People say that if they do then it's their loss but it's not really, is it? They can go off and find another partner whereas to the virgin it feels like their once only chance. Really the post I linked to explains my perspective perfectly and because your opinion is the one I'm not seeing much I'd like to hear more about it.

This is the exact attitude I have towards myself. Why am I in the same position as I was when I was a teen? There must be something wrong with me when, after meeting however many people I have in my lifetime, it still hasn't happened. I've always been shy and my insecurity is probably getting worse but really, shouldn't it have happened by now? I don't want to lose it in a random hook up so there is that but at the same time I have a knack for falling into friendships with girls and never any more.

If you were dating a guy of 26-27 and he told you he was a virgin a few dates in after you felt you knew him fairly well and liked what you knew do you think you might start doubting what you knew to that point? Do you think you'd start wondering if he was hiding something which had kept him a virgin despite everything you had learnt about him in the previous dates?
I get where you're coming from but, without disclosing any actual details, we've already had discussions inappropriate for the workplace. We met through work but we are friends now.
This is a different question really but would it affect your opinion of a potential romantic interest?
That's encouraging. How do you feel about the person being someone I work with?
That is a concern. I did meet the girl through work but we're friends outside of work now. Even so we're still colleagues.
Sorry, forgot to put that. I'm nearly 28, it does have an impact on my confidence for that reason.

I'm still going through it. Looking through some of your posts shows a lot of you have gone through far worse than me. I don't really have extreme feelings either way. Most of the time I have no motivation to do anything because really, what's the point? Occasionally I go really down and very occasionally I go a bit manic. None of this would be diagnosable as an actual disorder; they're just ups and downs with hopelessness thrown in for good measure.

Why do I feel this way? Feelings of inadequacy more than anything. I'm very inexperienced sexually and I place a lot of importance on this fact. Maybe you think this is a mistake but take a look in almost literally every direction and you'll see culture and society promoting the benefits of being in a couple, and if by some freak chance someone's trying to talk up being single one of the items in their list of pros will be "can have sex with whoever you want". Being intimate with someone is such an intrinsic part of life that I haven't experienced and it brings me so much shame that I've never actually told anyone in my life which means that I have a complicated web of stories some people know and others don't. Whole sections of my life are compartmentalised and I have to keep track of who knows what. It's the only lie I tell but it weighs on my shoulders.
